source.text:
The `@read` and `@write` ACL categories do not currently include `select`. This may be very confusing and may lead to non-obvious outcomes, since specifying the correct database is a fundamental requirement of successful read and write operations, and can lead to confusion, as demonstrated by [tickets like this](https://github.com/StackExchange/StackExchange.Redis/issues/2835) where the user had configured:

```
ACL SETUSER cacheUser on >myPass ~AppCache* -@all +@pubsub +@read +@write +echo +info +SET +GET +eval +ping
```

In the above case, the `-@all @read +@write` had the effect that `GET`, `SET` etc worked, but the `SELECT` did not, causing activity to happen incorrectly on DB0. Obviously a workaround here is to add `+select`, but I propose that this should be implicit in `@read` / `@write`.

Additional: I note that `select` *is* in `@keyspace` (which also includes things like `flushdb`, so: use-with-caution). I do not know whether there are implementation details that may cause problems such as "a command can only be in a single ACL category" (edit: upon further investigation I do not believe this to be a problem - `del` is in both `@write` and `@keyspace`, for example).

One potential gotcha; I do not know the order in which ACLs are applied; if it is left-to-right, then pre-existing setups like `+select +@read -@write` would presumably (if `select` was included in `@read` and `@write`) lead to not having `select`. Not sure if this is considered a problem. 

[Inherited documentation, not issue-author text: redis/redis-doc@7277deb0a858a6384d8a069fc654c61fcda32b34]
D1 topics/acl.md:
Such rules are always implemented from the
first to the last, left-to-right, because sometimes the order of the rules is
important to understand what the user is really able to do.
`+<command>`: Add the command to the list of commands the user can call.
`-<command>`: Remove the command to the list of commands the user can call.
`+@<category>`: Add all the commands in such category to be called by the user
`-@<category>`: Like `+@<category>` but removes the commands from the list of commands the client can call.
D2 commands/acl-setuser.md:
`+@<category>`: add all the commands in the specified category to the list of commands the user is able to execute.
`-@<category>`: Like `+@<category>` but removes all the commands in the category instead of adding them.
D3 commands/select.md:
Select the Redis logical database having the specified zero-based numeric index.
New connections always use the database 0.
When using Redis Cluster, the `SELECT` command cannot be used, since Redis Cluster only supports database zero.
Since the currently selected database is a property of the connection, clients should track the currently selected database and re-select it on reconnection.

obligations.statement: Keep the membership change narrow and preserve inherited processing rather than adding a new permission-precedence policy. The named mixed configuration may lose SELECT permission as the ordinary consequence of the requested membership addition.

unspecified: Nonblocking uncertainty: reporter Redis version is not identified. Evidence is an exact pre-issue documentation revision, not an empirical release matrix. No later-version or different ACL-rule-family behavior is certified.
No new ACL reload, migration, historical-user conversion, durable state, restart or retroactive membership-update policy. Configure fresh users in the experiment; no rollout guarantee.

No exact success/error wire spelling, invalid-index/syntax/authentication policy or concurrency/transaction behavior specified. Permission denial is distinct from successful selection; unrelated validation is not relaxed.
No changes to key access, authentication, other category memberships or commands are requested; no unrestricted key access inferred from SELECT permission.

Modules, alternate selectors, first-argument/subcommand rules, cluster mode and universal version compatibility are outside this bounded interpretation; expanding scope requires fresh evidence and review.
implementation_choices: Internal data structures, lookup and compilation strategy are free if the observable documented-rule processing and requested membership change are preserved.
Available nonzero database index, matching probe key and marker values are fixture choices, not product constants.
Effective permission precedence and rule-order outcomes are fixed behavior, not implementation freedoms.
